newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's TIM looks to French cellular market.
newsitem.headline: Italy's TIM looks to French cellular market.

text.p: Italy mobile phone operator, Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM), said it had decided to buy from its parent Stet a 49 percent stake in Stet Mobile Holding, giving it a potential foothold in the French cellular phone market.
As part of a recent deal between Italian state telecoms group Stet and France's Bouygues, a Bouygues unit took a 19.6 percent stake in Stet Mobile Holding.
"With the aquisition of 49 percent of Stet Mobile Holding, TIM will be preparing itself to enter the important French cellular phone market," TIM said in a statement.
TIM did not say how much it would pay for the holding or when the sale would go through.
In the same statement, TIM said its digital GSM service chalked up just over a 100 billion lire operating result in the first nine months of the year.
It said it now had 1.3 million GSM clients with 260,000 new clients signing up in the last month alone.
Adding its TAC service to the calculations, it said it had more than 5.1 million clients, making it the largest mobile phone operator in Europe and the third largest in the world.
It said TIM now controlled 68.5 percent of the whole GSM market -- up 4 percent on September levels.
TIM competes in the Italian GSM market against Omnitel, controlled by information and technology group Olivetti.
It has a monopoly in the domestic TAC market.
